text.p: Tallinna Pank said on Thursday it bought the majority of shares in Lithuanian brokerage company Baltijos Vertyviniai Popieriai for 80,000 litas.
"It is slightly above its accounting value," Targo Raus, vice council head of the bank, told Reuters.
"Their balance sheet was clear and transparent," Raus said, adding the company was itself ready for cooperation.
He added that Tallinna opted for BVP also as the sum involved in the deal was not large.
"It is one of the most orderly brokerages on the Lithuanian market, although not among the largest," Raus added.
Tallinna Pank plans to reorganise the company's management to a certain extent and wants it to become a part of the bank's network of the Baltic brokerage companies, Raus said.
"We will develop the best brokerage company in Lithuania, which will trade in Tallinn, Riga and Vilnius," he added.
Raus said Tallinna Pank is also working on launching a brokerage house in Latvia.
Tallinna Pank received the license to purchase 74 percent of the Lithuanian company on Thursday.
The minority stake of BVP is held by the insurance company Baltijas Garanta.
